text_blocks.snippet: To travel to Afghanistan, foreign nationals generally need to obtain an Afghan visa. Following the 2021 Taliban takeover, visa issuance has become more complex, with some diplomatic missions ceasing visa issuance while others continue. For those seeking visas, options may include applying in countries like Dubai or Peshawar (Pakistan).
snippet_highlighted_words: foreign nationals generally need to obtain an Afghan visa

list.title: Visa Requirement:
list.snippet: Afghanistan requires visas for most foreign visitors.

list.title: Visa Issuance:
list.snippet: Some Afghan diplomatic missions abroad continue to issue visas, while others have stopped.

list.title: Application Locations:
list.snippet: Applying for a visa can be done in specific locations like Dubai or Peshawar, with other options available in neighboring countries.

list.title: Recent Changes:
list.snippet: In June 2022, the Taliban government stated that anyone can visit Afghanistan for humanitarian activities or tourism, according to a government spokesman.

list.title: Special Immigrant Visas (SIVs):
list.snippet: There are also special immigrant visas for Afghans who worked for the U.S. government, their families, or other eligible individuals.

list.title: Resettlement:
list.snippet: Afghan nationals paroled into the United States may be eligible for resettlement benefits, and can contact local resettlement agencies for information.

list.title: Visa Types:
list.snippet: Afghanistan offers various visa types, including tourist, entry for work permit, resident, transit, double entry, diplomatic, service, student, and exit visas, {according to Fast Passports & Visas https://fastpassportsandvisas.com/visas/us/afghanistan/}.

list.title: Required Documents:
list.snippet: Documents typically needed include a valid passport, passport photos, and potentially an invitation letter or other supporting documents depending on the visa type.
